title: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (California, 2019) (case summary)
text: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (case summary): the driver was wildfire ignited by utility equipment; the exposed assets were electricity transmission and distribution network; the event took place in North America in 2019.
lessons: Utility wildfire liability can exceed equity, so the binding constraint becomes liquidity and a legislated backstop rather than the physical repair bill.
Insurers who paid claims returned as subrogation claimants, so the insured loss turned into a claim on the utility.
driver: wildfire ignited by utility equipment
assets: electricity transmission and distribution network

title: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (California, 2019) — PG&E Form 8-K, 9 December 2019
text: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (PG&E Form 8-K, 9 December 2019): PG&E Corporation and Pacific Gas and Electric Company began Chapter 11 cases on 29 January 2019.

title: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (California, 2019) — PG&E Form 8-K, 9 December 2019
text: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (PG&E Form 8-K, 9 December 2019): PG&E agreed a settlement valued at approximately $13.5 billion with the Official Committee of Tort Claimants and firms representing individual claimants from the 2015 Butte Fire, the 2017 Northern California wildfires and the 2018 Camp Fire.

title: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (California, 2019) — PG&E Form 8-K, 9 December 2019
text: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (PG&E Form 8-K, 9 December 2019): PG&E had earlier agreed an $11 billion settlement with insurance companies and other entities that had already paid claims for the 2017 and 2018 wildfires, and a $1 billion settlement with cities, counties and other public entities.

title: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (California, 2019) — PG&E Form 8-K, 9 December 2019
text: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (PG&E Form 8-K, 9 December 2019): PG&E said it had received over $12 billion of equity backstop commitments to support the settlement and its plan of reorganization.

title: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (California, 2019) — PG&E Form 8-K, 9 December 2019
text: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (PG&E Form 8-K, 9 December 2019): PG&E needed to emerge from Chapter 11 by 30 June 2020, the statutory deadline under Assembly Bill 1054 to participate in California's go-forward wildfire fund.

title: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (California, 2019) — PG&E Form 8-K, 9 December 2019
text: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (PG&E Form 8-K, 9 December 2019), response (financial): PG&E settled with each major claimant group, which fixed the total wildfire liability before the plan was finalised.

title: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (California, 2019) — PG&E Form 8-K, 9 December 2019
text: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (PG&E Form 8-K, 9 December 2019), response (financial): PG&E lined up more than $12 billion of equity backstop commitments to fund the settlements.

title: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (California, 2019) — PG&E Form 8-K, 9 December 2019
text: PG&E wildfire liabilities and Chapter 11 (PG&E Form 8-K, 9 December 2019), response (policy): California created a go-forward wildfire fund under Assembly Bill 1054, and PG&E timed its emergence from Chapter 11 to qualify for it.

event_name: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue
title: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (2023 to 2025) (case summary)
text: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (case summary): the driver was higher interest rates, supply-chain delays and unadjusted power-price contracts on US offshore wind; the exposed assets were US offshore wind development portfolio; the event took place in Europe and North America in 2023.
lessons: A fixed-price offtake contract with a long build period turns interest-rate and supply-chain moves into impairments, even for a technology that policy supports.
Transition winners can still fail financially when contract prices cannot adjust to input costs.
driver: higher interest rates, supply-chain delays and unadjusted power-price contracts on US offshore wind
assets: US offshore wind development portfolio

event_name: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue
title: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (2023 to 2025) — Ørsted company announcement, 31 October 2023
text: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (Ørsted company announcement, 31 October 2023): Ørsted recognised impairments of DKK 28.4 billion in the interim report for the first nine months of 2023, of which DKK 19.9 billion related to Ocean Wind 1.

event_name: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue
title: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (2023 to 2025) — Ørsted company announcement, 31 October 2023
text: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (Ørsted company announcement, 31 October 2023): Ørsted had announced on 29 August 2023 anticipated US impairments of up to DKK 16 billion; later adverse developments in supply chains, higher interest rates and the lack of an OREC adjustment on Sunrise Wind raised the total.

event_name: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue
title: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (2023 to 2025) — Ørsted company announcement, 31 October 2023
text: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (Ørsted company announcement, 31 October 2023): Ørsted decided to cease development of Ocean Wind 1 and 2 and estimated a provision of approximately DKK 8 to 11 billion for potential contract cancellation fees on Ocean Wind 1.

event_name: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue
title: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (2023 to 2025) — Ørsted company announcement, 31 October 2023
text: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (Ørsted company announcement, 31 October 2023): Ørsted took the final investment decision on the 704 MW Revolution Wind project, owned 50/50 with Eversource, while recording a DKK 3.3 billion impairment on it.

event_name: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue
title: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (2023 to 2025) — Ørsted investor page on the 2025 rights issue
text: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (Ørsted investor page on the 2025 rights issue): Ørsted completed a rights issue in October 2025 that raised DKK 60 billion in gross proceeds.

event_name: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue
title: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (2023 to 2025) — Ørsted investor page on the 2025 rights issue
text: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (Ørsted investor page on the 2025 rights issue): The 2025 rights issue proceeds were to cover the incremental funding requirement from retaining full ownership of Sunrise Wind in the US.

event_name: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue
title: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (2023 to 2025) — Ørsted company announcement, 31 October 2023
text: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (Ørsted company announcement, 31 October 2023), response (strategic): Ørsted ceased development of Ocean Wind 1 and 2 after supplier delays, changed tax-credit and permit assumptions, and higher long-dated US interest rates worsened the business case.

event_name: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue
title: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (2023 to 2025) — Ørsted company announcement, 31 October 2023
text: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (Ørsted company announcement, 31 October 2023), response (financial): Ørsted announced cost savings, working-capital improvements such as supply chain financing, prioritised development activity and portfolio rationalisation to protect its capital structure and credit rating.

event_name: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue
title: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (2023 to 2025) — Ørsted investor page on the 2025 rights issue
text: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (Ørsted investor page on the 2025 rights issue), response (financial): Ørsted raised DKK 60 billion through a rights issue in October 2025 to strengthen its capital structure.

event_name: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue
title: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (2023 to 2025) — Ørsted company announcement, 31 October 2023
text: Ørsted US offshore wind impairments and rights issue (Ørsted company announcement, 31 October 2023), response (strategic): Ørsted continued Revolution Wind into construction and said it would assess whether to rebid Sunrise Wind at a price that reflects current component and financing costs.

event_name: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water
title: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water (Germany) (case summary)
text: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water (case summary): the driver was prolonged low river levels during the 2018 drought; the exposed assets were Ludwigshafen chemical complex supplied by barge on the Rhine; the event took place in Europe in 2018.
lessons: A chronic hazard such as low river water acts through logistics and throughput, and its cost is rarely a single line item.
The earnings hit was mixed with unrelated market margin changes, so attributing it to the climate hazard needs the company's own estimate.
driver: prolonged low river levels during the 2018 drought
assets: Ludwigshafen chemical complex supplied by barge on the Rhine

event_name: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water
title: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water (Germany) — BASF news release, 26 October 2018
text: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water (BASF news release, 26 October 2018): BASF said the low water level in the Rhine River had an impact on business throughout the entire third quarter of 2018, leading to production cutbacks and higher transportation costs.

event_name: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water
title: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water (Germany) — BASF news release, 26 October 2018
text: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water (BASF news release, 26 October 2018): BASF Group EBIT before special items in the third quarter of 2018 was €1.5 billion, down €232 million, mainly because of a significantly lower contribution from the Chemicals segment.

event_name: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water
title: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water (Germany) — BASF news release, 26 October 2018
text: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water (BASF news release, 26 October 2018): In the Chemicals segment, EBIT before special items fell by €251 million to €851 million, primarily because of lower margins for isocyanates and steam cracker products, and higher fixed costs.

event_name: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water
title: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water (Germany) — BASF news release, 26 October 2018
text: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water (BASF news release, 26 October 2018): BASF net income in the third quarter of 2018 declined by €136 million to €1.2 billion.

event_name: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water
title: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water (Germany) — ChemAnager, 10 December 2018
text: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water (ChemAnager, 10 December 2018): On 7 December 2018 BASF cut its outlook and said low Rhine water in the fourth quarter of 2018 was expected to cause negative earnings impacts of up to €200 million.

event_name: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water
title: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water (Germany) — BASF news release, 26 October 2018
text: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water (BASF news release, 26 October 2018), response (operational): BASF cut production at Ludwigshafen and paid higher transport costs to move goods when barges could not load fully.

event_name: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water
title: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water (Germany) — ChemAnager, 10 December 2018
text: BASF and the 2018 low Rhine water (ChemAnager, 10 December 2018), response (disclosure): BASF quantified the low-water effect at about €50 million in the third quarter and up to €200 million in the fourth, then lowered its full-year outlook.

event_name: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market
title: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (2021) (case summary)
text: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (case summary): the driver was extreme cold causing generator and gas-supply outages; the exposed assets were power generators, retail electricity providers and cooperatives in the ERCOT market; the event took place in North America in 2021.
lessons: Generators with fixed-price obligations lost cash on a price spike, while the market's default rules pushed unpaid balances onto everyone else.
Securitization turned a one-off liquidity shock into a long-dated charge on customers.
driver: extreme cold causing generator and gas-supply outages
assets: power generators, retail electricity providers and cooperatives in the ERCOT market

event_name: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market
title: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (2021) — Power Engineering, 28 April 2021
text: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (Power Engineering, 28 April 2021): ERCOT reported close to 52 GW of power generation outages from weatherization issues, impaired gas delivery and other factors during Winter Storm Uri.

event_name: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market
title: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (2021) — Power Engineering, 28 April 2021
text: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (Power Engineering, 28 April 2021): Vistra estimated that the financial impact of Winter Storm Uri cost the company about $1.6 billion in cash flow.

event_name: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market
title: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (2021) — Power Engineering, 28 April 2021
text: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (Power Engineering, 28 April 2021): NRG Energy reported close to $1 billion in negative impact to cash flow from the storm.

event_name: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market
title: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (2021) — Power Engineering, 28 April 2021
text: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (Power Engineering, 28 April 2021): Brazos Electric Cooperative filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in March 2021 because of its financial hit from the storm.

event_name: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market
title: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (2021) — Vistra Form 10-Q, June 2023
text: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (Vistra Form 10-Q, June 2023): ERCOT was left roughly $2.9 billion short after the storm, mostly because of Brazos, and filed a claim of about $1.9 billion against Brazos.

event_name: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market
title: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (2021) — Vistra Form 10-Q, June 2023
text: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (Vistra Form 10-Q, June 2023): Vistra recognised a default uplift liability of approximately $189 million in the first quarter of 2021, later reduced to $124 million as ERCOT collected from defaulting entities through other means, primarily securitization.

event_name: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market
title: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (2021) — The Bond Buyer
text: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (The Bond Buyer): Texas authorised ERCOT to recover $2.1 billion of upfront storm costs through securitization, and cooperatives could securitize their share of the unpaid balance, about $2.5 billion, with 30-year bonds.

event_name: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market
title: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (2021) — The Bond Buyer
text: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (The Bond Buyer), response (financial): Texas spread the unpaid market balances over 30 years through securitization charges billed to customers.

event_name: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market
title: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (2021) — Vistra Form 10-Q, June 2023
text: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (Vistra Form 10-Q, June 2023), response (financial): ERCOT and Brazos mediated rather than spreading the default across all participants, and settled in September 2022.

event_name: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market
title: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (2021) — The Bond Buyer
text: Winter Storm Uri and the Texas power market (The Bond Buyer), response (policy): Texas adopted grid weatherization measures and securitization legislation after the storm.

event_name: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains
title: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains (case summary)
text: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains (case summary): the driver was the worst flooding in Thailand in more than 50 years; the exposed assets were industrial estates north of Bangkok producing hard drives, electronics and auto parts; the event took place in Asia in 2011.
lessons: Component plants concentrated in one flood plain shut down downstream assembly lines in other countries even though the assembly plants stayed dry.
Contingent business interruption, not the repair bill, drove the loss for firms that depended on a single industrial park.
driver: the worst flooding in Thailand in more than 50 years
assets: industrial estates north of Bangkok producing hard drives, electronics and auto parts

event_name: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains
title: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains — Business Insurance
text: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains (Business Insurance): Insurance claims from the 2011 Thailand floods had reached about $3.3 billion, against estimated economic damage of roughly $5 billion.

event_name: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains
title: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains — Business Insurance
text: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains (Business Insurance): The floods reached 61 of Thailand's 77 provinces, breached defences around seven industrial parks and affected about 1,300 factories.

event_name: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains
title: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains — Supply Chain Digital
text: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains (Supply Chain Digital): Toyota stopped production at three Thai plants, and a Honda production centre with capacity for 120,000 vehicles a year, outside Bangkok, was closed from 4 October.

event_name: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains
title: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains — Supply Chain Digital
text: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains (Supply Chain Digital): Analysts forecast that Thai auto production would fall by about 130,000 units in 2011 because of the flooding.

event_name: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains
title: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains — Supply Chain Digital
text: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains (Supply Chain Digital), response (operational): Western Digital relied on its plants in Malaysia, Singapore and the United States while the Thai plants were shut.

event_name: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains
title: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains — Law Journal Newsletters, January 2012
text: 2011 Thailand floods and the electronics and auto supply chains (Law Journal Newsletters, January 2012), response (transfer): Western Digital filed an insurance claim expected to lower the net impact of its flood damage.

event_name: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers
title: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers (2018) (case summary)
text: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers (case summary): the driver was typhoon storm surge and wind in the Osaka Bay area; the exposed assets were Kansai International Airport and property across the Kansai region; the event took place in Asia in 2018.
lessons: Early insured-loss estimates for the same event differed widely between modellers, and the tally of claims later exceeded their central estimates.
Reinsurance absorbed the largest share of an insurer's gross loss, which is why the insurers stayed profitable while the lower reinsurance layers were used up.
driver: typhoon storm surge and wind in the Osaka Bay area
assets: Kansai International Airport and property across the Kansai region

event_name: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers
title: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers (2018) — Business Insurance
text: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers (Business Insurance): RMS estimated Japan's insured loss from Typhoon Jebi at between $3 billion and $5.5 billion, with about 80% of the loss in the Kansai region.

event_name: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers
title: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers (2018) — Reinsurance News
text: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers (Reinsurance News): The operator of Kansai airports reported Jebi-related disaster losses of ¥8.1 billion in fiscal 2018 and received disaster insurance proceeds of ¥6.2 billion, recovering more than 75% of the loss.

event_name: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers
title: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers (2018) — Intelligent Insurer
text: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers (Intelligent Insurer): Moody's expected Tokio Marine, Sompo and MS&AD to remain profitable for the full fiscal year, and noted that multiple catastrophes had exhausted the lower layers of catastrophe excess-of-loss cover for some Japanese insurers.

event_name: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers
title: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers (2018) — Reinsurance News
text: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers (Reinsurance News), response (transfer): The airport operator recovered most of its loss through disaster insurance proceeds.

event_name: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers
title: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers (2018) — Intelligent Insurer
text: Typhoon Jebi, Kansai airport and Japanese insurers (Intelligent Insurer), response (transfer): Japanese insurers passed more than half of their gross 2018 typhoon losses to reinsurers.

title: July 2021 European floods (Germany's Ahr valley) and the insurance gap (case summary)
text: July 2021 European floods (case summary): the driver was record rainfall from low-pressure system Bernd causing flash floods; the exposed assets were homes, railways, roads and bridges in Germany and neighbouring countries; the event took place in Europe in 2021.
lessons: Where flood cover is rare and the damage is to public infrastructure, insured loss is a minor share of economic loss, so insurer results understate the hit to the economy.
Early modelled insured-loss estimates for this event were later revised sharply upward.
driver: record rainfall from low-pressure system Bernd causing flash floods
assets: homes, railways, roads and bridges in Germany and neighbouring countries

title: July 2021 European floods (Germany's Ahr valley) and the insurance gap — Insurance Business, reporting Munich Re's 2021 review
text: July 2021 European floods (Insurance Business, reporting Munich Re's 2021 review): Munich Re put total losses from the July 2021 European floods at €46 billion, of which €33 billion was in Germany.

title: July 2021 European floods (Germany's Ahr valley) and the insurance gap — Insurance Business, reporting Munich Re's 2021 review
text: July 2021 European floods (Insurance Business, reporting Munich Re's 2021 review): More than 220 people were killed in the floods.

title: July 2021 European floods (Germany's Ahr valley) and the insurance gap — Insurance Business, reporting Munich Re's 2021 review
text: July 2021 European floods (Insurance Business, reporting Munich Re's 2021 review): Munich Re attributed the low insured share to uninsured infrastructure losses and the limited insurance density for flooding in Germany.

title: July 2021 European floods (Germany's Ahr valley) and the insurance gap — Verisk, July 2021 European floods
text: July 2021 European floods (Verisk, July 2021 European floods): An early Verisk estimate in July 2021 said insured losses in Germany would approach €5 billion, well below the later €8.2 billion industry figure.

title: July 2021 European floods (Germany's Ahr valley) and the insurance gap — Insurance Business, reporting Munich Re's 2021 review
text: July 2021 European floods (Insurance Business, reporting Munich Re's 2021 review), response (transfer): Insured households and businesses were paid by German insurers, but most of the €33 billion German loss fell on uninsured owners, infrastructure and the public sector.

event_name: Hawaiian Electric and the Maui wildfire
title: Hawaiian Electric and the Maui wildfire (2023) (case summary)
text: Hawaiian Electric and the Maui wildfire (case summary): the driver was wildfire in a drought-and-wind event on Maui; the exposed assets were Hawaiian Electric's distribution network and its balance sheet; the event took place in North America in 2023.
lessons: A liability sized well above the equity value pushes the borrower to junk ratings, which closes capital markets just when cash is needed for the settlement.
driver: wildfire in a drought-and-wind event on Maui
assets: Hawaiian Electric's distribution network and its balance sheet

event_name: Hawaiian Electric and the Maui wildfire
title: Hawaiian Electric and the Maui wildfire (2023) — Gulf News / AP
text: Hawaiian Electric and the Maui wildfire (Gulf News / AP): Hawaiian Electric's share of the Maui settlement was almost $2 billion.

event_name: Hawaiian Electric and the Maui wildfire
title: Hawaiian Electric and the Maui wildfire (2023) — Gulf News / AP
text: Hawaiian Electric and the Maui wildfire (Gulf News / AP): The fire caused Hawaiian Electric's parent to lose more than half of its market value, and its credit ratings were cut to junk.

event_name: Hawaiian Electric and the Maui wildfire
title: Hawaiian Electric and the Maui wildfire (2023) — Gulf News / AP
text: Hawaiian Electric and the Maui wildfire (Gulf News / AP), response (financial): Hawaiian Electric agreed to a settlement share of almost $2 billion, which avoided a heftier liability that could have forced it into bankruptcy.

event_name: Hawaiian Electric and the Maui wildfire
title: Hawaiian Electric and the Maui wildfire (2023) — The Bond Buyer
text: Hawaiian Electric and the Maui wildfire (The Bond Buyer), response (financial): S&P later called the settlement supportive of credit quality because it potentially limited the company's litigation exposure.

event_name: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies
title: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies (2022 to 2023) (case summary)
text: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies (case summary): the driver was rising wildfire exposure, rebuilding costs and inflation against regulated prices; the exposed assets were California homes and the mortgage and property markets that depend on insurance; the event took place in North America in 2023.
lessons: When regulated premiums cannot rise with modelled risk, insurers restrict supply, which pushes homeowners to the residual market and can lower property values.
driver: rising wildfire exposure, rebuilding costs and inflation against regulated prices
assets: California homes and the mortgage and property markets that depend on insurance

event_name: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies
title: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies (2022 to 2023) — ABC7 News
text: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies (ABC7 News): State Farm, California's largest carrier, stopped issuing new homeowner policies in the state in late May 2023, citing mounting disaster exposure, rebuilding costs and inflation.

event_name: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies
title: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies (2022 to 2023) — ABC7 News
text: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies (ABC7 News): Allstate confirmed in June 2023 that it had stopped writing new homeowner, condominium and commercial policies in California the previous year.

event_name: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies
title: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies (2022 to 2023) — ABC7 News
text: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies (ABC7 News): Allstate said the cost to insure new California home customers was far higher than the price they would pay for policies.

event_name: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies
title: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies (2022 to 2023) — ABC7 News
text: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies (ABC7 News): State Farm and Allstate said they were still serving existing customers, and more than 100 other insurers were still issuing new homeowner policies in California.

event_name: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies
title: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies (2022 to 2023) — ABC7 News
text: State Farm and Allstate stop writing new California homeowners policies (ABC7 News), response (strategic): Insurers stopped writing new business rather than exit the market entirely, keeping existing customers.

title: Panama Canal drought restrictions (2023 to 2024) (case summary)
text: Panama Canal drought restrictions (case summary): the driver was severe drought worsened by El Niño lowering the lakes that feed the locks; the exposed assets were the Panama Canal and the shipping lines that use it; the event took place in Latin America in 2023.
lessons: A water-dependent chokepoint turns a drought into a throughput limit that is priced through queues and slot auctions, so the cost lands on shippers rather than on one asset owner.
driver: severe drought worsened by El Niño lowering the lakes that feed the locks
assets: the Panama Canal and the shipping lines that use it

title: Panama Canal drought restrictions (2023 to 2024) — Inquirer / AFP
text: Panama Canal drought restrictions (Inquirer / AFP): Authorities restricted the Panama Canal to ships with a maximum draft of 13.11 metres, or 43 feet, amid a severe drought.

title: Panama Canal drought restrictions (2023 to 2024) — Inquirer / AFP
text: Panama Canal drought restrictions (Inquirer / AFP): Daily crossings fell from an average of 40 ships a day in 2022 to 32 to save water.

title: Panama Canal drought restrictions (2023 to 2024) — Inquirer / AFP
text: Panama Canal drought restrictions (Inquirer / AFP): About 130 boats were waiting on one day in August 2023, compared with around 90 usually in the queue.

title: Panama Canal drought restrictions (2023 to 2024) — Inquirer / AFP
text: Panama Canal drought restrictions (Inquirer / AFP): Waiting times, usually between three and five days, rose to 19 days at times.

title: Panama Canal drought restrictions (2023 to 2024) — Inquirer / AFP
text: Panama Canal drought restrictions (Inquirer / AFP): The Panama Canal moves about six percent of the world's maritime commerce.

title: Panama Canal drought restrictions (2023 to 2024) — Inquirer / AFP
text: Panama Canal drought restrictions (Inquirer / AFP), response (operational): Ships could reserve a slot in advance or buy one through an auction process.

title: Panama Canal drought restrictions (2023 to 2024) — Inquirer / AFP
text: Panama Canal drought restrictions (Inquirer / AFP), response (operational): The canal operator capped daily transits and draft, then raised the quotas as rain returned in early 2024.

title: Taiwan's 2021 drought and chipmakers (case summary)
text: Taiwan's 2021 drought and chipmakers (case summary): the driver was a drought after no monsoon rains refilled reservoirs; the exposed assets were semiconductor fabs that use large volumes of water; the event took place in Asia in 2021.
lessons: A water-intensive asset can avoid output loss in a drought by paying for trucked water, so the cost shows up as a small operating expense rather than as lost sales.
driver: a drought after no monsoon rains refilled reservoirs
assets: semiconductor fabs that use large volumes of water

title: Taiwan's 2021 drought and chipmakers — Fortune, 12 June 2021
text: Taiwan's 2021 drought and chipmakers (Fortune, 12 June 2021): TSMC said it began reducing water use and trucking water to some facilities in February 2021, and that so far there was no impact on production.

title: Taiwan's 2021 drought and chipmakers — Fortune, 12 June 2021
text: Taiwan's 2021 drought and chipmakers (Fortune, 12 June 2021): An average semiconductor factory consumes roughly 20,000 tons of water a day, according to China Water Risk.

title: Taiwan's 2021 drought and chipmakers — Fortune, 12 June 2021
text: Taiwan's 2021 drought and chipmakers (Fortune, 12 June 2021): Taiwan's government began rationing water as the island experienced no monsoon rains for the first time since the 1950s.

title: Taiwan's 2021 drought and chipmakers — Fortune, 12 June 2021
text: Taiwan's 2021 drought and chipmakers (Fortune, 12 June 2021), response (operational): TSMC trucked in water and cut its own water use as a precaution, and said production was not affected.

event_name: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines
title: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines (2024) (case summary)
text: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines (case summary): the driver was historic drought reducing hydropower at Lake Kariba; the exposed assets were Zambian copper mines and smelters that depend on hydroelectric power; the event took place in Africa in 2024.
lessons: Mines that depend on one hydro basin can keep operating by importing power at a higher price, so the cost moves into operating margins even when output holds.
driver: historic drought reducing hydropower at Lake Kariba
assets: Zambian copper mines and smelters that depend on hydroelectric power

event_name: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines
title: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines (2024) — Mining Weekly, 13 September 2024
text: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines (Mining Weekly, 13 September 2024): Hydropower supplies roughly 85% of Zambia's electricity, and a historic drought undercut that supply in 2024.

event_name: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines
title: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines (2024) — Mining Weekly, 13 September 2024
text: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines (Mining Weekly, 13 September 2024): Households in Zambia were getting about three hours of electricity a day in September 2024.

event_name: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines
title: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines (2024) — Mining Weekly, 13 September 2024
text: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines (Mining Weekly, 13 September 2024): Zambia was weeks away from having to shut Kariba down completely for the first time for lack of water.

event_name: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines
title: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines (2024) — Mining Weekly, 13 September 2024
text: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines (Mining Weekly, 13 September 2024): Eskom's transmission unit began supplying 250 MW to Zambia in August 2024, more than 10% of Zambia's normal national demand.

event_name: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines
title: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines (2024) — Miningmx
text: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines (Miningmx): First Quantum's Kansanshi and Sentinel operations were receiving about 285 MW, which allowed normal operations at the Kansanshi mine and smelter.

event_name: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines
title: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines (2024) — Mining Weekly, 13 September 2024
text: Kariba drought and Zambian copper mines (Mining Weekly, 13 September 2024), response (operational): First Quantum sourced power from neighbouring countries and expected supply to its mines and smelters to continue uninterrupted.

event_name: 2015 Chennai floods and the auto cluster
title: 2015 Chennai floods and the auto cluster (India) (case summary)
text: 2015 Chennai floods and the auto cluster (case summary): the driver was heaviest rainfall in a century in Tamil Nadu; the exposed assets were auto assembly plants and suppliers in the Chennai cluster; the event took place in Asia in 2015.
lessons: Short plant outages can be partly recovered with overtime, so the loss depends on how long the closure lasts and whether suppliers are also flooded.
driver: heaviest rainfall in a century in Tamil Nadu
assets: auto assembly plants and suppliers in the Chennai cluster

event_name: 2015 Chennai floods and the auto cluster
title: 2015 Chennai floods and the auto cluster (India) — Business Today, 2 December 2015
text: 2015 Chennai floods and the auto cluster (Business Today, 2 December 2015): Hyundai, Ford and Renault-Nissan suspended production in Chennai on 2 December 2015 after rain flooded their sites or cut off their workers.

event_name: 2015 Chennai floods and the auto cluster
title: 2015 Chennai floods and the auto cluster (India) — Carrier Management, 7 December 2015
text: 2015 Chennai floods and the auto cluster (Carrier Management, 7 December 2015): Insurers expected about 10 billion rupees in immediate claims, with most coming from residents who lost property such as vehicles.

event_name: 2015 Chennai floods and the auto cluster
title: 2015 Chennai floods and the auto cluster (India) — Business Today, 2 December 2015
text: 2015 Chennai floods and the auto cluster (Business Today, 2 December 2015), response (operational): Hyundai and other makers worked extra shifts, including Sundays, to make up the lost production.

event_name: Valencia DANA floods and Spain's Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros
title: Valencia DANA floods and Spain's Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros (2024) (case summary)
text: Valencia DANA floods and Spain's Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros (case summary): the driver was an isolated high-level depression (DANA) causing extreme rainfall around Valencia; the exposed assets were homes, cars and businesses covered by the state insurance consortium; the event took place in Europe in 2024.
lessons: A public reinsurer with a large pre-funded reserve absorbs the tail, so private insurers keep only a small share, but the reserve must be rebuilt with higher rates afterwards.
driver: an isolated high-level depression (DANA) causing extreme rainfall around Valencia
assets: homes, cars and businesses covered by the state insurance consortium

event_name: Valencia DANA floods and Spain's Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros
title: Valencia DANA floods and Spain's Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros (2024) — Guy Carpenter, November 2024
text: Valencia DANA floods and Spain's Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros (Guy Carpenter, November 2024): The Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros had received more than 138,000 claims by 8 November 2024, including more than 43,000 for residential dwellings and more than 83,000 for motor vehicles.

event_name: Valencia DANA floods and Spain's Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros
title: Valencia DANA floods and Spain's Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros (2024) — Guy Carpenter, November 2024
text: Valencia DANA floods and Spain's Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros (Guy Carpenter, November 2024): The Consorcio estimated it would cover 90 to 95% of the claims in the region for €3.5 billion, with the remaining €250 to 300 million incurred by primary insurers.

event_name: Valencia DANA floods and Spain's Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros
title: Valencia DANA floods and Spain's Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros (2024) — DBRS Morningstar
text: Valencia DANA floods and Spain's Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros (DBRS Morningstar): DBRS expected total insured losses, including Consorcio-covered amounts, to exceed €4 billion.

event_name: Valencia DANA floods and Spain's Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros
title: Valencia DANA floods and Spain's Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros (2024) — DBRS Morningstar
text: Valencia DANA floods and Spain's Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros (DBRS Morningstar), response (policy): The Consorcio covers catastrophic events automatically, so no disaster declaration was needed, and private insurers worked with it to speed claims.

event_name: Cyclone Idai and the port of Beira
title: Cyclone Idai and the port of Beira (Mozambique, 2019) (case summary)
text: Cyclone Idai and the port of Beira (case summary): the driver was tropical cyclone landfall at Beira; the exposed assets were the Beira port, including the Vale and Rio Tinto coal terminal; the event took place in Africa in 2019.
lessons: Preparation protected the movable equipment, but buildings and the single rail link remained the weak points for trade through the corridor.
driver: tropical cyclone landfall at Beira
assets: the Beira port, including the Vale and Rio Tinto coal terminal

event_name: Cyclone Idai and the port of Beira
title: Cyclone Idai and the port of Beira (Mozambique, 2019) — Swedish Club
text: Cyclone Idai and the port of Beira (Swedish Club): Cornelder, which runs the port, said advance preparation meant the port sustained only limited damage, though the general cargo warehouses had severe roof damage.

event_name: Cyclone Idai and the port of Beira
title: Cyclone Idai and the port of Beira (Mozambique, 2019) — Mining Monthly
text: Cyclone Idai and the port of Beira (Mining Monthly): Vale uses 68 percent of the Beira coal terminal's capacity and Rio Tinto uses 32 percent.

event_name: Cyclone Idai and the port of Beira
title: Cyclone Idai and the port of Beira (Mozambique, 2019) — Swedish Club
text: Cyclone Idai and the port of Beira (Swedish Club), response (operational): The port operator tied down the gantry cranes and prepared in advance, so the cranes withstood the storm.

title: Rio Grande do Sul floods (Brazil, 2024) (case summary)
text: Rio Grande do Sul floods (case summary): the driver was unprecedented flooding in Rio Grande do Sul in April and May 2024; the exposed assets were steel plants, auto plants, farms, roads, an airport and bank loan books in the state; the event took place in Latin America in 2024.
lessons: Logistics damage affects every firm in a region, not only those flooded, and banks with concentrated regional loan books carry credit exposure that is invisible in a plant-level view.
driver: unprecedented flooding in Rio Grande do Sul in April and May 2024
assets: steel plants, auto plants, farms, roads, an airport and bank loan books in the state

title: Rio Grande do Sul floods (Brazil, 2024) — AP, 23 May 2024
text: Rio Grande do Sul floods (AP, 23 May 2024): The National Confederation of Municipalities estimated financial losses from the Rio Grande do Sul floods at about 10 billion reais, roughly $1.9 billion.

title: Rio Grande do Sul floods (Brazil, 2024) — AP, 23 May 2024
text: Rio Grande do Sul floods (AP, 23 May 2024): The state's industry federation estimated that about 94% of the state's economic activity had been disrupted in some way.

title: Rio Grande do Sul floods (Brazil, 2024) — Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance
text: Rio Grande do Sul floods (Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance), response (operational): Gerdau stopped the affected steel units and General Motors suspended its plant until the water receded.

event_name: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant
title: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant (Texas, 2017) (case summary)
text: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant (case summary): the driver was record flooding from Hurricane Harvey; the exposed assets were the Arkema organic peroxide plant in Crosby and the Houston Ship Channel petrochemical complex; the event took place in North America in 2017.
lessons: Backup power that shares the flood exposure of the primary supply is not independent protection, and the loss then comes from the hazardous inventory rather than the water.
driver: record flooding from Hurricane Harvey
assets: the Arkema organic peroxide plant in Crosby and the Houston Ship Channel petrochemical complex

event_name: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant
title: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant (Texas, 2017) — CBC
text: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant (CBC): Flooding overwhelmed the Arkema Crosby plant's primary power supply and two emergency backups, so it lost refrigeration for its organic peroxides.

event_name: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant
title: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant (Texas, 2017) — CBC
text: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant (CBC): Arkema's North America CEO said the plant would almost certainly explode, and two trailers of unstable compounds later blew up and burned.

event_name: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant
title: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant (Texas, 2017) — CBC
text: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant (CBC): Authorities set a 2.4 kilometre area around the plant and up to 5,000 nearby residents were warned to evacuate.

event_name: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant
title: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant (Texas, 2017) — Chemistry World
text: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant (Chemistry World): Of the 132 petrochemical sites along the Houston Ship Channel, at least one-third and up to half were offline.

event_name: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant
title: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant (Texas, 2017) — CBC
text: Hurricane Harvey and the Arkema Crosby plant (CBC), response (operational): Arkema pulled its employees, warned residents and the authorities, and let the stored peroxides burn once refrigeration could not be restored.

event_name: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage
title: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage (2017) (case summary)
text: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage (case summary): the driver was Category 4 hurricane destroying Puerto Rico's electricity grid; the exposed assets were Baxter's three Puerto Rico IV-fluid plants and the island's pharmaceutical and device plants; the event took place in North America in 2017.
lessons: A single-site product made in a hurricane zone becomes a national shortage, whereas firms with redundant sites reported no patient impact.
driver: Category 4 hurricane destroying Puerto Rico's electricity grid
assets: Baxter's three Puerto Rico IV-fluid plants and the island's pharmaceutical and device plants

event_name: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage
title: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage (2017) — WGBH, 6 December 2017
text: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage (WGBH, 6 December 2017): Hurricane Maria wiped out Puerto Rico's electrical grid and shut Baxter's three Puerto Rico factories for several days.

event_name: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage
title: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage (2017) — WGBH, 6 December 2017
text: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage (WGBH, 6 December 2017): About ten weeks after the storm one Baxter factory was still powered by a diesel generator while the other two were back on the grid, with intermittent power.

event_name: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage
title: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage (2017) — FDA Law Blog
text: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage (FDA Law Blog): Pharmaceutical manufacturing represented 72% of Puerto Rico's exports in 2016, worth $14.5 billion.

event_name: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage
title: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage (2017) — WGBH, 6 December 2017
text: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage (WGBH, 6 December 2017), response (operational): Baxter ran its plants on generators and rationed product by past purchase volume.

event_name: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage
title: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage (2017) — WGBH, 6 December 2017
text: Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico and the US IV-bag shortage (WGBH, 6 December 2017), response (policy): The FDA permitted imports from other manufacturers and extended expiry dates to relieve the shortage.

event_name: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned
title: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned (Netherlands, 2021 to 2024) (case summary)
text: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned (case summary): the driver was a court order that a company cut emissions including customers' emissions; the exposed assets were Shell's oil and gas strategy and production plans; the event took place in Europe in 2021.
lessons: Even a reversed climate ruling shows the legal channel: a court can in principle set targets for a company, which creates a contingent cost of capex and production change that is hard to price.
driver: a court order that a company cut emissions including customers' emissions
assets: Shell's oil and gas strategy and production plans

event_name: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned
title: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned (Netherlands, 2021 to 2024) — NPR / KPBS, 12 November 2024
text: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned (NPR / KPBS, 12 November 2024): In May 2021 a Hague district court ordered Shell to cut its CO2 emissions by 45% by 2030 relative to 2019, including emissions from customers' use of its products.

event_name: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned
title: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned (Netherlands, 2021 to 2024) — NPR / KPBS, 12 November 2024
text: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned (NPR / KPBS, 12 November 2024): Shell's own target at the time was a 50% cut against 2016 levels covering only scope 1 and 2 emissions.

event_name: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned
title: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned (Netherlands, 2021 to 2024) — NPR / KPBS, 12 November 2024
text: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned (NPR / KPBS, 12 November 2024): In November 2024 the Court of Appeal in The Hague overturned the order, finding it could not establish that a duty of care required a 45% cut or some other percentage.

event_name: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned
title: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned (Netherlands, 2021 to 2024) — NPR / KPBS, 12 November 2024
text: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned (NPR / KPBS, 12 November 2024): The appeals court said Shell has a duty to reduce its emissions and is already doing so, and that Shell may decide how to make the cuts.

event_name: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned
title: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned (Netherlands, 2021 to 2024) — NPR / KPBS, 12 November 2024
text: Milieudefensie v. Shell: court-ordered emissions cuts overturned (NPR / KPBS, 12 November 2024), response (strategic): Shell appealed, kept its net-zero-by-2050 goal and its plan to halve operational emissions by 2030, and left the choice of methods to itself.

event_name: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap
title: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap (Swiss Re sigma) (case summary)
text: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap (case summary): the driver was growth in exposure and secondary perils such as severe convective storms; the exposed assets were insured and uninsured property worldwide; the event took place in Global in 2025.
lessons: Because most economic loss is uninsured, the cost of climate events lands on households, firms and governments, not only on insurers.
driver: growth in exposure and secondary perils such as severe convective storms
assets: insured and uninsured property worldwide

event_name: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap
title: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap (Swiss Re sigma) — Swiss Re Institute sigma 1/2025
text: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap (Swiss Re Institute sigma 1/2025): Swiss Re Institute put global insured natural catastrophe losses in 2024 at $137 billion and total economic losses at $318 billion, of which 57% were uninsured.

event_name: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap
title: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap (Swiss Re sigma) — Swiss Re Institute sigma 1/2025
text: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap (Swiss Re Institute sigma 1/2025): The 2024 protection gap was $181 billion.

event_name: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap
title: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap (Swiss Re sigma) — Swiss Re Institute sigma 1/2025
text: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap (Swiss Re Institute sigma 1/2025): Swiss Re Institute said insured natural catastrophe losses continue to grow at 5 to 7% a year in real terms, which would take them toward $145 billion in 2025.

event_name: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap
title: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap (Swiss Re sigma) — Swiss Re Institute press release on 2025
text: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap (Swiss Re Institute press release on 2025): Swiss Re Institute reported 2025 economic losses of $220 billion, about 49% of them insured, and insured losses of $107 billion, below the long-term trend.

event_name: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap
title: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap (Swiss Re sigma) — Swiss Re Institute press release on 2025
text: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap (Swiss Re Institute press release on 2025): Wildfires, storms and floods, mainly secondary perils, made up a record 92% of global insured losses in 2025.

event_name: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap
title: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap (Swiss Re sigma) — Swiss Re Institute sigma 1/2025
text: Global natural-catastrophe losses and the insurance protection gap (Swiss Re Institute sigma 1/2025), response (transfer): Insurers and reinsurers priced the trend into premiums and attachment points, while most losses in poorer markets stayed uninsured.

event_name: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in
title: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in (Canada, 2016) (case summary)
text: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in (case summary): the driver was wildfire that forced evacuation and shut-in of oil sands operations; the exposed assets were oil sands mining, upgrading and the Syncrude joint venture; the event took place in North America in 2016.
lessons: An evacuation can idle productive assets for weeks without large physical damage, so the loss arrives as lost output and higher unit costs rather than a repair bill.
driver: wildfire that forced evacuation and shut-in of oil sands operations
assets: oil sands mining, upgrading and the Syncrude joint venture

event_name: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in
title: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in (Canada, 2016) — Engineering News, 29 July 2016
text: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in (Engineering News, 29 July 2016): Suncor reported a second-quarter 2016 operating loss of $565 million and a net loss of $735 million, driven by the shut-in of oil sands production because of the forest fires and low crude prices.

event_name: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in
title: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in (Canada, 2016) — Engineering News, 29 July 2016
text: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in (Engineering News, 29 July 2016): Suncor's oil sands cash operating costs rose to $46.80 a barrel in the second quarter from $28.00 a barrel a year earlier.

event_name: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in
title: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in (Canada, 2016) — Engineering News, 29 July 2016
text: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in (Engineering News, 29 July 2016): By mid-July 2016 production at all of Suncor's oil sands operations had returned to normal.

event_name: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in
title: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in (Canada, 2016) — Engineering News, 29 July 2016
text: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in (Engineering News, 29 July 2016): Syncrude, a joint venture in which Suncor holds an interest, was completely shut down in early May 2016 for the first time in its 40-year history and returned to normal in mid-July.

event_name: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in
title: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in (Canada, 2016) — Engineering News, 29 July 2016
text: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in (Engineering News, 29 July 2016): The fires also paused work at the Fort Hills oil sands mining project, which Suncor owns 51% with Total 29% and Teck 20%.

event_name: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in
title: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in (Canada, 2016) — Engineering News, 29 July 2016
text: Fort McMurray wildfire and Suncor oil sands shut-in (Engineering News, 29 July 2016), response (operational): Suncor and Syncrude restarted oil sands operations in stages and had them back at normal output by mid-July 2016.

event_name: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses
title: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses (New Zealand, 2023) (case summary)
text: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses (case summary): the driver was extreme rainfall flooding and a tropical cyclone over the North Island; the exposed assets were homes, businesses, vehicles and rural infrastructure; the event took place in Oceania in 2023.
lessons: A first-quarter estimate of claims moved sharply as claims matured, so early loss figures understate the final bill.
Large events in a small insurance market can change reinsurance availability and price for the whole country.
driver: extreme rainfall flooding and a tropical cyclone over the North Island
assets: homes, businesses, vehicles and rural infrastructure

event_name: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses
title: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses (New Zealand, 2023) — Insurance Council of New Zealand, March 2023
text: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses (Insurance Council of New Zealand, March 2023): The Insurance Council of New Zealand recorded more than 40,000 Cyclone Gabrielle claims worth about NZ$890 million in March 2023, of which about NZ$70 million had been paid.

event_name: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses
title: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses (New Zealand, 2023) — Insurance Council of New Zealand, March 2023
text: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses (Insurance Council of New Zealand, March 2023): Hawke's Bay recorded more than 13,000 claims worth over NZ$481 million, more than half of the total value to date.

event_name: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses
title: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses (New Zealand, 2023) — Insurance Business, Suncorp CEO on reinsurers
text: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses (Insurance Business, Suncorp CEO on reinsurers): Suncorp's chief executive said reinsurers had been unprepared for the scale of the Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle, raising concern that they might leave the New Zealand market.

event_name: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses
title: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses (New Zealand, 2023) — Insurance Business, Suncorp CEO on reinsurers
text: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses (Insurance Business, Suncorp CEO on reinsurers), response (transfer): Suncorp secured its reinsurance programme after the events, at a higher cost.

event_name: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses
title: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses (New Zealand, 2023) — The Insurer on IAG
text: Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle insured losses (The Insurer on IAG), response (financial): IAG took the claims hit in its results and raised its natural perils allowance.

event_name: KwaZulu-Natal floods and the Durban port
title: KwaZulu-Natal floods and the Durban port (South Africa, 2022) (case summary)
text: KwaZulu-Natal floods and the Durban port (case summary): the driver was extreme rainfall and flooding in KwaZulu-Natal; the exposed assets were Durban port terminals, rail and road access; the event took place in Africa in 2022.
lessons: Port operations can restart quickly while the road and rail links that feed them stay damaged, so throughput recovers more slowly than the headline reopening.
driver: extreme rainfall and flooding in KwaZulu-Natal
assets: Durban port terminals, rail and road access

event_name: KwaZulu-Natal floods and the Durban port
title: KwaZulu-Natal floods and the Durban port (South Africa, 2022) — News24, 13 April 2022
text: KwaZulu-Natal floods and the Durban port (News24, 13 April 2022): Transnet suspended operations across its Durban terminals on 11 April 2022 as a precaution.

event_name: KwaZulu-Natal floods and the Durban port
title: KwaZulu-Natal floods and the Durban port (South Africa, 2022) — Sowetan, 21 April 2022
text: KwaZulu-Natal floods and the Durban port (Sowetan, 21 April 2022): Transnet said long-term recovery measures could take as long as 12 months.

event_name: KwaZulu-Natal floods and the Durban port
title: KwaZulu-Natal floods and the Durban port (South Africa, 2022) — Sowetan, 21 April 2022
text: KwaZulu-Natal floods and the Durban port (Sowetan, 21 April 2022), response (operational): Transnet reopened the port within days and then restored road and rail access in stages over the following weeks.

event_name: Tata Steel Port Talbot electric arc furnace and UK grant
title: Tata Steel Port Talbot electric arc furnace and UK grant (United Kingdom, 2024) (case summary)
text: Tata Steel Port Talbot electric arc furnace and UK grant (case summary): the driver was decarbonisation of blast-furnace steelmaking supported by a government grant; the exposed assets were blast furnaces at Port Talbot and the workforce that runs them; the event took place in Europe in 2024.
lessons: A transition investment can depend on public funding and on grid connection timing, so delay risk sits with infrastructure the company does not control.
driver: decarbonisation of blast-furnace steelmaking supported by a government grant
assets: blast furnaces at Port Talbot and the workforce that runs them

event_name: Tata Steel Port Talbot electric arc furnace and UK grant
title: Tata Steel Port Talbot electric arc furnace and UK grant (United Kingdom, 2024) — The Chemical Engineer
text: Tata Steel Port Talbot electric arc furnace and UK grant (The Chemical Engineer): About 2,500 jobs will still be lost as Tata closes the site's only remaining blast furnace.

event_name: Tata Steel Port Talbot electric arc furnace and UK grant
title: Tata Steel Port Talbot electric arc furnace and UK grant (United Kingdom, 2024) — The Chemical Engineer
text: Tata Steel Port Talbot electric arc furnace and UK grant (The Chemical Engineer): Tata Steel must retain 5,000 employees across its UK operations as a condition of the grant.

event_name: Tata Steel Port Talbot electric arc furnace and UK grant
title: Tata Steel Port Talbot electric arc furnace and UK grant (United Kingdom, 2024) — Maritime Gateway, September 2026
text: Tata Steel Port Talbot electric arc furnace and UK grant (Maritime Gateway, September 2026): Tata Steel was reported in September 2026 to be seeking fresh UK government funding because delays in securing a grid connection had pushed commissioning of the furnace to late 2028 or early 2029.

event_name: Tata Steel Port Talbot electric arc furnace and UK grant
title: Tata Steel Port Talbot electric arc furnace and UK grant (United Kingdom, 2024) — Machinery.co.uk, September 2024
text: Tata Steel Port Talbot electric arc furnace and UK grant (Machinery.co.uk, September 2024), response (strategic): Tata Steel replaced coke-fired blast furnaces with scrap-based electric arc steelmaking, using a government grant to cover part of the capital cost.

event_name: UK December freeze and Aviva weather claims
title: UK December freeze and Aviva weather claims (United Kingdom, 2022) (case summary)
text: UK December freeze and Aviva weather claims (case summary): the driver was a December cold snap causing burst pipes and property claims; the exposed assets were insured homes and commercial property in the UK; the event took place in Europe in 2022.
lessons: A single cold spell can be material for one insurer's quarter even when the full year stays near its weather average.
driver: a December cold snap causing burst pipes and property claims
assets: insured homes and commercial property in the UK

event_name: UK December freeze and Aviva weather claims
title: UK December freeze and Aviva weather claims (United Kingdom, 2022) — Reinsurance News, Aviva December freeze
text: UK December freeze and Aviva weather claims (Reinsurance News, Aviva December freeze): Aviva estimated the cost of December 2022 freezing weather in the UK at about £50 million.

event_name: UK December freeze and Aviva weather claims
